Round 14 · The rebuild, measured against the real thing

Look first. Measure second.

R14 added a fourth stage — a green forest that reads unmistakably as the arcade’s — and halved the oldest crack: a do-nothing stick now gets ~10 gun kills in 90 s, down from ~20. It rises to 8.3. But the two combat illusion-breakers only improved, they didn’t close: pointing the gun at the enemies still doesn’t out-kill a dead stick, and a missile lock is now available every wave but a human still can’t always convert it. Both trace to one keystone — the sight can’t reach where it needs to.
“Two real reproduced gains — the blind gun halved and a fourth stage — against two headline combat illusion-breakers that improved but did not close. Pointing the gun where the planes are still didn’t beat a dead-centre stick; the missile lock exists now but a human can’t always convert it.”

Ours vs the arcade

stage 1 · 60 Hz capture vs mapped longplay

Shipped this round

held up under the judge’s re-measure
  • A 4th stage — the green forest (arcade stage 4), palette measured; stages 1–3 regression-free
  • The blind gun HALVED — a do-nothing stick gets ~10 gun kills/90 s, down from ~20 (reproduced both seeds)
  • Missile lock now AVAILABLE every other wave, including the adverse seed that fired nothing before
  • The death-cycle argument SETTLED with data — arcade deaths re-measure at ~8.1 s, the cycle is correct

Next — R15

ranked by what breaks the illusion
  1. 01 FEEL
    The sight can’t reach where it needs to (the keystone)

    Both combat residuals reduce to one fact: the sight can’t dip to the low close jets (gun) or climb high enough to centre the lock cone on the bait (missile). Give it more vertical reach — but MEASURE the arcade’s vertical sight range first (it has no arcade column yet), and check the gun actually converts, because the judge pushed the sight down and still lost to a blind stick.

  2. 02 FEEL
    The gun kills by supply, not by aim

    Aiming still doesn’t out-kill a dead stick (9 vs 10 even with the sight shoved onto the enemy row). The cap is as much target SUPPLY — too few close targets — and the wide hit net, as it is reach. This is the same problem as density below.

  3. 03 MISSING
    The sky is too even — no wall, no lull

    The arcade is a wall of planes at every depth, then empties; ours holds a steady ~3–6. The burst-then-drought rhythm is missing, and it’s also what would give the gun close targets to aim at.

  4. 04 MISSING
    Breadth — 4 of 23 stages, no resupply or bonus

    Four biomes now, but the resupply/bonus passes and the rest of the 23 stages remain the biggest structural absence. Keep chipping.

  5. 05 POLISH
    Forest ground, climaxes, title

    The stage-4 forest reads darker/flatter than the arcade’s bright mottled canopy; kill fireballs still read sub-screen; the title wordmark is hand-rounded where the arcade’s is brush-angular.

Keep — do not regress

  • The 4th stage and stages 1–3 (no regression); the afterburner flame across all four
  • The blind-gun floor halved; missile availability every other wave; blind-pilot protection
  • The flyby, live sky, enemies through respawn; the game-over path; ±60° attract drama
  • The death cycle at ~8 s (arcade-confirmed — do NOT shorten it)

R14 settled a three-round-old argument with data — the ‘death cycle too long’ complaint was re-measured on real arcade deaths (~8.1 s) and confirmed correct, so it’s closed for good. The combat lane also declined to hack a cross-lane lever and wrote a precise ask instead, naming the keystone the next round opens on. History in judging/R14/.
